ceremony.title: Ceremony type
ceremony.description: Choose how you'd like to marry. You can change it whenever you like.
ceremony.disclaimer: This is a guide and may vary by town or region. Confirm the details with your Civil Registry, notary or parish.

toasts.error: We couldn't save the ceremony type.

civil.label: Civil
civil.tagline: Performed by a civil authority, with full legal validity.
implies: It's officiated by an authority: a mayor or councillor, a justice of the peace, a notary or a court clerk.
You first need to process the marriage file (at the Civil Registry or with a notary).
It's usually short and can be held at the town hall, the court, the notary's office or, depending on the municipality, another agreed venue.
civil.legal: The marriage is entered in the Civil Registry and is legal from that moment.

religiosa.label: Religious
religiosa.tagline: Held according to the rite of a religious denomination.
implies: It's officiated by whoever applies in your denomination (priest, pastor, rabbi, imam…).
In the Catholic Church there is a file at the parish, a baptism certificate and, usually, a pre-marriage course.
Timing and venue depend on the parish or community: it's best to talk to them early.
religiosa.legal: A Catholic ceremony has civil effects if it's registered at the Civil Registry (usually handled by the parish). Other denominations with an agreement with the State (Evangelical, Jewish, Islamic) can also have them, with their own requirements.

simbolica.label: Symbolic
simbolica.tagline: A ceremony tailored to you, with no legal effect on its own.
implies: You choose the place, the readings, the rituals and who officiates, with no mandatory script.
It doesn't change your marital status and isn't entered in any register.
It can be held on the same day as the civil wedding or on another date.
simbolica.legal: It has no legal validity on its own. For the marriage to be legal you also need a civil wedding (or a religious one with civil effects).
simbolica.legalBadge: A civil wedding is also needed

legal.title: Legal documents
legal.description: A guide to the paperwork and procedures for getting married in Spain.

disclaimer.title: A guide only: confirm with your Civil Registry.
disclaimer.text: Requirements vary by municipality, notary or parish, and this guide does not replace their official information.

noType.title: First, choose the ceremony type
noType.text: The paperwork is different for a civil, religious or symbolic wedding. Once you choose, you'll see the list that applies to you here.

intro.symbolic: A symbolic ceremony has no legal validity on its own, so this list is the one for a civil wedding: it's the one that makes your marriage valid in law.
intro.religious: This list is for a Catholic ceremony. If yours is a different denomination, ask your community what they require and whether you need to get a certificate of legal capacity to marry from the Civil Registry first.
intro.civil: This is the list for a civil wedding in Spain. Each Civil Registry or notary may ask for a little more or less.

foreign.label: One of you is a foreign national or has documents from another country
foreign.hint: This adds apostilled and translated documents and the certificate of legal capacity to marry.

previous.label: One of you has been married before
previous.hint: This adds the certificate of the previous marriage showing the divorce, annulment or death.

groups.foreign: If there are documents from another country
groups.previous: If there was a previous marriage

cita.title: Book an appointment at the Civil Registry or a notary
cita.hint: This is the first step. It's done at the Civil Registry of either partner's home address, or with a notary.

dni.title: Valid ID card, NIE or passport for both of you
dni.hint: Check they won't expire before the wedding.

nacimiento.title: Full birth certificate
nacimiento.hint: Request it online from the Ministry of Justice e-office or at the Civil Registry. It usually has to be recent.

empadronamiento.title: Certificate of residence (empadronamiento)
empadronamiento.hint: Issued by the town hall (often online). It tells you which Civil Registry is yours.

declaracion.title: Sworn statement of marital status
declaracion.hint: Each person declares their marital status and that there is no impediment to marrying. Usually signed when the file is opened.

testigos.title: Details of two adult witnesses
testigos.hint: Full name and ID number. Ask whether they must attend the file hearing or only the wedding.

resolucion.title: Favourable decision on the file
resolucion.hint: This is the document that allows you to marry. It's only valid for a limited time: check yours before setting the date.

parroquia.title: Talk to the parish or community and set a date
parroquia.hint: This is the first step: they will tell you what they require and how far ahead.

dni.title: Valid ID card, NIE or passport for both of you
dni.hint: Check they won't expire before the wedding.

nacimiento.title: Full birth certificate
nacimiento.hint: Request it online from the Ministry of Justice e-office or at the Civil Registry. It usually has to be recent.

bautismo.title: Recent baptism certificate
bautismo.hint: From the parish where each of you was baptised. Ask for it with annotations; it usually has to be from the last few months.

confirmacion.title: Confirmation certificate
confirmacion.hint: Only if your parish asks for it.

cursillo.title: Pre-marriage course
cursillo.hint: Talks run by parishes and dioceses. Places fill up: sign up early and keep the attendance certificate.

expediente-parroquial.title: Marriage file at the parish
expediente-parroquial.hint: An interview with the officiant and signing of the documents. The parish processes it with the bishopric.

empadronamiento.title: Certificate of residence (empadronamiento)
empadronamiento.hint: Some parishes ask for it to decide which one should marry you.

inscripcion.title: Registration at the Civil Registry after the wedding
inscripcion.hint: This is what gives it civil effects. Ask the parish whether it handles it and when you'll get the certificate.

ext-capacidad.title: Certificate of legal capacity to marry or of marital status from the country of origin
ext-capacidad.hint: Issued by the country's authority or consulate. Ask what your Civil Registry accepts.

ext-apostilla.title: Foreign documents with an apostille or legalised
ext-apostilla.hint: The Hague apostille makes them valid in Spain. It's arranged in the country that issued them.

ext-traduccion.title: Sworn translation of any documents not in Spanish
ext-traduccion.hint: It must be done by a sworn translator. Allow a few days.

ext-residencia.title: Proof of residence in Spain (NIE or registration certificate)
ext-residencia.hint: Only if you live in Spain and don't have a DNI.

matrimonio-anterior.title: Full certificate of the previous marriage noting the divorce, annulment or death
matrimonio-anterior.hint: Request it at the Civil Registry where it was registered. If the divorce was in another country, you'll need that document apostilled and translated.

sentencia.title: Divorce ruling or agreement, or death certificate
sentencia.hint: If requested, in addition to the previous certificate.
